sources.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
Audi boss under fire in Germany for Trump rally appearance

en.title: Audi to invest $4bn in Georgia factory, announces at Trump rally
en.dek: Audi announced a $4bn investment to build a factory in Georgia, creating 4,500 jobs, during a rally with former President Trump.
facts: Audi will build its first US factory near Macon, Georgia, at a cost of $4bn (€3.6bn) and create 4,500 jobs (DW).
Construction will begin next year, with production of up to 200,000 SUVs annually starting in the early 2030s (DW).
Audi CEO Gernot Döllner appeared with Trump at a rally in Perry, Georgia, to announce the investment (Guardian).
Trump said the tariffs contributed to Audi's decision to invest (DW).
Audi said the investment is a long‑term commitment to the US premium market (DW).
body: Audi announced a $4bn investment to build its first US factory near Macon, Georgia, creating 4,500 jobs (DW). The plant will produce up to 200,000 premium SUVs annually, with construction starting next year and production beginning in the early 2030s (DW). The announcement was made during a rally in Perry, Georgia, where CEO Gernot Döllner appeared with former President Donald Trump (Guardian). Döllner said the investment is a long‑term commitment to the US premium market (DW).

The German government declined to comment, calling the move a business decision (Guardian). The Social Democratic Party’s transport spokesperson Isabel Cademartori called the appearance a disgrace, citing VW’s Nazi history (Guardian). Union leaders IG Metall’s Christiane Benner called the appearance embarrassing and politically unacceptable (Guardian). VW works council chief Daniela Cavallo said Döllner had become a puppet in Trump’s propaganda show (Guardian).

Audi said the 15% tariffs on European vehicles cost it €1.2bn last year (DW). The investment is intended to avoid or reduce those tariffs, according to industry analysts (DW). German automakers face pressure from China, rising costs, and conflicts, and have issued profit warnings (DW). Volkswagen plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs by 2030, while Audi’s Neckarsulm plant faces closure risk (DW).

The deal has drawn criticism in Germany for linking a business decision to a political event (Guardian). Audi maintains the investment is driven by growth and resilience, not by tariffs (DW). The plant will be Audi’s first US factory, a first for a premium brand (DW). The investment reflects broader shifts in the auto industry toward domestic production in the US (DW).
en.context: German automakers are under pressure from Chinese competitors and rising costs, prompting profit warnings and job cuts (DW). Audi’s decision to build a US plant follows the 15% tariff on European cars imposed by Trump (DW). The investment aims to secure a foothold in the US premium market (DW).
